intelligence.essence: Creation, push-button simple: this family closes the batch with the Factory judged by whether other Nayas can build from it, the activation manual it needed, the reusable-parts law underneath, and the whole picture assembled — universal app, onboarding, Factory and Project Intelligence as one flow, ending in the manual-alone proof and the Smart-Note habit that feeds it all. The standard is a stranger test: a Naya with only the manual and the parts should produce the real thing, first try, without a rescue thread. Where she can't, the gap is the Factory's defect, named and counted — six of them, in this family, by name.
intelligence.human_view: A recipe is only a good recipe if someone else can cook from it. The great test of a cookbook is handing it to a stranger and tasting what they make. If they stall at 'prepare the pan', the recipe was missing a step — you don't blame the cook, you fix the book.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine you write instructions for your friend to build your Lego castle, then you go outside. If she builds it perfectly — your instructions were great! If she gets stuck, you don't say she's bad at Lego. You fix the instructions so the next friend can do it.
intelligence.grandma_view: When I taught my granddaughter to knit, I watched her hands, not my own. Every place she tangled was a place my teaching had skipped a stitch. Good teachers and good manuals share that rule: the learner's stall is the teacher's homework.
intelligence.ai_view: Ship the manual section with the capability, same job. Run manual-alone proofs with genuinely fresh builders and file stalls as Factory defects. Compose from inventoried parts; file any newly built part into the Factory before closing the job.
intelligence.what_it_means: A factory is not its machines; it is the repeatability of its output in other hands. The activation manual is therefore not documentation about the Factory — it is part of the Factory, the part that travels. The manual-alone proof is the honest audit of that claim: hand the manual to a fresh builder, watch where she stalls, and file the stalls as Factory defects rather than builder failures. That inversion — the system owns the gaps — is what makes the next builder faster instead of just more careful.

page.machine: 1) Every Factory capability ships with its activation manual section; a capability without one is unfinished. 2) The manual-alone proof is run for each new capability: a fresh builder, manual only, gaps filed as Factory defects with names and counts. 3) Builds compose reusable parts under the parts law; a build that invents a part files the part into the Factory as part of the same job. 4) The creation flow is one flow: universal app + onboarding + Factory + Project Intelligence, push-button simple at the citizen's end.
page.why_it_matters: NayaNET's promise is that citizens — and Nayas — build worlds in minutes. That promise is exactly as strong as the manual-alone proof and no stronger. This essence keeps the proof standing, so 'push-button simple' remains a measured property of the system instead of a sentence in a deck.
page.how_it_connects: This essence is batch 8's E10 panel; its raw family spans SN-2577 to SN-2586 (The Factory — Can Other Nayas Build From It? → The Smart-Note Habit), and it sits in the standing sequence of sixty essences that came before it — each one checked against the census coverage map for zero overlap before it was written.
page.what_is_in_it_for_you: For you, Shawn, this means this stratum of the record no longer has to be re-read note by note: its law is stated once, whole, in words a cold reader can use — and the hundred raw notes beneath it are accounted for, by number, in the Distills line.
page.the_learning: A factory is proven in other hands: manual alone, fresh builder, real output — and every stall she hits is the Factory's defect, not hers.
